subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing recurring-cron cadence guardrail, with unset/0 preserving current behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast jobs?
rationale: This adds a new core config surface and configured fail-closed behavior for schedules that are valid today, which is a product and compatibility choice beyond ordinary code correctness.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Docs Fix
options.body: Keep the core config surface, require the docs-map refresh and fresh exact-head checks, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Prefer Warning-Only Behavior
options.body: Reject configured enforcement for now and pursue an advisory warning path if maintainers do not want scheduled jobs rejected or paced.

options.title: Defer Core Config
options.body: Pause or close this PR until the broader cron/session accumulation issue is split into narrower guardrail and retention decisions.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Docs Fix
recommendation.body: Keep the core config surface, require the docs-map refresh and fresh exact-head checks, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.
